title: Claude Cowork is now your Chrome side panel
format_note: One task told as a single scripted screen story: click the extension, type a prompt, watch tabs get worked through, receive a spreadsheet. No voice, music bed only.
one_thing: Claude in Chrome's side panel can take one plain-English instruction and carry it across ten open tabs into a finished spreadsheet.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. YouTube had no caption track; local whisper returned only 'Music' cues at 0-2 s and 30-38 s.
transcript.script_shape: All meaning is carried by 10 words of title and CTA copy plus the product's own UI text: prompt, status lines, reply and spreadsheet.

structure.frame0: Cream ground, one line of near-black serif: 'Claude Cowork is now your Chrome side panel', 6 words, about 6.7% of frame height, centred (f0001.jpg). Subject named, product not yet shown.
structure.first_3s: Title holds about 2.25 s, then dissolves word by word left to right over about 0.7 s (strips/window-02-2.125s.jpg), blank at 2.96 s, hard cut at 3.0 s to a browser window on sage green.

beats.what: Title card states the news: Cowork is now a Chrome side panel.
Browser window on sage plate, ten tabs, a rent statement; cursor drifts to the top right.
Cut to a crop of the toolbar; cursor clicks the Claude asterisk; the Claude tab group lights up orange.
Side panel slides in beside the page; camera pushes down into its message box.
Prompt types in: 'Run my month-end close on these tabs...'; cursor clicks send at 14.4 s.
Panel shows the user bubble and 'Writing.'; camera pulls back to the full window.
Claude hops tab to tab (utility, courier, waste invoices) under a pale red edge glow and a Stop Claude pill.
Scene moves to the Cowork desktop window with Progress, Outputs, Claude in Chrome rows; text 'Running command...'.
Reply lists July total $10,017.80 and four flags; an Invoice Log spreadsheet panel slides in with status pills.
'Try it now: claude.com/chrome' alone on cream, drifts up and out.
Asterisk grows from a dot, the word 'Claude' types in beside it, holds, music stops at 39.7 s.

hero_moment.what: The finished Invoice Log spreadsheet beside Claude's reply: totals, ten vendors, coloured status pills (f0016.jpg). It is the payoff of the instruction typed at 10 s.

ending.what: CTA card of 4 words at about 6.8% height, then a typed-in Claude wordmark on cream held to the last frame.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Four cuts in the first 4.2 s (3.0, 5.08, 5.96, 7.17) set up the story, then one at 14.5 and one at 19.33. After that camera moves and UI changes carry it; the last detected shot is 21.9 s (53% of runtime). No burst.

product_ui.notes: Fictional vendors and .example domains, so the UI is staged. Toolbar, prompt and status pills are large in crop; the reply paragraph and invoice rows are about 1.8% of frame height and would not read on a phone.

motion.eases: Not measured numerically. In the strips, title words fade out in order over about 0.7 s and the CTA lifts about 22 px while exiting at 36.75-37.0 s.

good.observation: Frame 0 is a finished poster: the news in one 6.7%-high serif line, centred, no logo or black. The title leaves in reading order, then the cut to the product follows at once.
Cuts follow the cursor: it heads to the toolbar and the film cuts to a close crop of the target; the click at 14.4 s cuts to the working panel at 14.5 s.
The prompt is shown in a large crop and typed live, so the one fact the viewer needs is readable at phone size before the camera pulls back.
Autonomy is shown without words: a pale red edge glow, a Stop Claude pill and tab-to-tab hops make 'it is working across your tabs' visible.
The proof is a concrete artifact: a ten-row invoice log with Pending, Overdue, Paid pills beside a reply quoting dollar figures.
The ending is quiet and complete: a 4-word CTA, then the mark builds from a dot and holds 3.3 s, with music out at 39.7 s.
Two grounds and one accent colour: cream for statements, sage for product, coral only on Claude elements. Scenes feel like one object.

weak.observation: The reply paragraph and invoice rows are about 13 px, 1.8% of frame height, held for 6 s or more; they cannot be read on a phone and carry the proof by texture alone.
The promised panel does not appear until about 7.2 s; the first 7 s are title, a rent statement and a cursor, so product payoff is late for a 41 s film.
